### Women’s Counter-Strike
Page: https://goat.biblioverse.org/en/#m/counter-strike-feminino
- GOAT: Ksenia “vilga” Klyuenkova (RU)
- Legends: Zainab “zAAz” Turkie (SE)
- Stars: Julia “juliano” Kiran (SE), ASTRA (FR)
- Other greats: Anna “Ant1ka” Ananikova (RU), Ana “ANa” Dumbravă (RO), Michaela “mimi” Lintrup (DK), Clara “Cla” Rossi (BR)
- Fact-check: medium

Ksenia “vilga” Klyuenkova is one of the most successful players in women’s Counter-Strike: she won ESWC 2016, WESG 2017 and ESL Impact seasons with Nigma Galaxy, and was among Russia’s best for more than a decade. In 2025, ASTRA was named HLTV’s best female player of the year, after winning ESL Impact with BIG EQUIPA.

Sources:
- [HLTV — prêmios femininos de 2025](https://www.hltv.org/news/43606/astra-and-big-equipa-secure-womens-awards)

### Men’s Counter-Strike
Page: https://goat.biblioverse.org/en/#m/counter-strike-masculino
- GOAT: Mathieu “ZywOo” Herbaut (FR)
- Legends: Nicolai “dev1ce” Reedtz (DK), Christopher “GeT_RiGhT” Alesund (SE), Marcelo “coldzera” David (BR), Oleksandr “s1mple” Kostyliev (UA), Danil “donk” Kryshkovets (RU)
- Stars: Olof “olofmeister” Kajbjer Gustafsson (SE), Filip “NEO” Kubski (PL), Nikola “NiKo” Kovač (BA), Gabriel “FalleN” Toledo (BR), Lukas “gla1ve” Rossander (DK), Dan “apEX” Madesclaire (FR), Ilya “m0NESY” Osipov (RU)
- Other greats: Kenny “kennyS” Schrub (FR), Ladislav “GuardiaN” Kovács (SK), Robin “flusha” Rönnquist (SE), Patrik “f0rest” Lindberg (SE), Yehor “markeloff” Markelov (UA), Martin “trace” Heldt (DK), Peter “dupreeh” Rasmussen (DK), Jonathan “EliGE” Jablonowski (US), Finn “karrigan” Andersen (DK), Raphael “cogu” Camargo (BR), Emil “HeatoN” Christensen (SE), Tommy “Potti” Ingemarsson (SE)
- Prospects: Dmitriy “sh1ro” Sokolov (RU), Helvijs “broky” Saukants (LV), David “frozen” Čerňanský (SK), Martin “stavn” Lund (DK)
- Fact-check: high

Mathieu “ZywOo” Herbaut is the GOAT of Counter-Strike. He is the only player named HLTV’s best player of the year four times (2019, 2020, 2023 and 2025), has three Major MVPs and 34 big-event MVPs — far ahead of anyone else — with a record eight MVPs in a single year (2025). Oleksandr “s1mple” Kostyliev once shared the spot, but stepped away from competition and returned at a lower level, while ZywOo has stayed at the top and kept collecting MVPs for years. Among in-game leaders, gla1ve (Astralis) and apEX (EnVyUs and Vitality) have four Majors each, and karrigan, champion in 2022 with FaZe and in 2026 with Falcons (at the Cologne Major, where m0NESY was MVP), became at 36 the oldest Major winner in history. The HLTV Hall of Fame, open only to players no longer active, includes HeatoN, Potti, GeT_RiGhT and f0rest (2024) and cogu, olofmeister and markeloff (2025) — cogu, a pioneer of the Brazilian scene, was the first from his country to be inducted.

### CrossFire
Page: https://goat.biblioverse.org/en/#m/crossfire
- GOAT: Wang “N9” Hao (CN)
- Legends: Zheng “Xxiao” Qi (CN)
- Stars: Chen “577” Jinwei (CN), Zhang “ZY” Ye (CN)
- Other greats: Willian “wil” Bello (BR), Carlos “vianna1” Vianna (BR), Daniel “DANIMAL” Polidoro (BR), Adriano “adrF” Soares (BR), Leonardo “nottziN” Dias (BR)
- Fact-check: medium

Wang “N9” Hao is considered the greatest player in CrossFire history: competing since 2015, he won CrossFire Stars, the game’s world championship, in 2016, 2017, 2022 and 2023 and, in 2026, won with BaiSha Gaming the only major title he was missing, the Esports World Cup, where he was named MVP. Zheng “Xxiao” Qi, his BaiSha teammate, is another of the biggest winners of the Chinese scene, which dominates the game. Brazil is the second power: in 2018, Black Dragons, with wil, vianna1, DANIMAL, adrF and nottziN, beat Russia’s ruLegends 3-0 in the final to become the first non-Chinese world champion, taking US$500,000; they were then runners-up in 2019 and third in 2020, and Vasco were runners-up in 2024. The most recent CrossFire Stars champions were Evolution Power Gaming (2024) and All Gamers (2025).

- [Liquipedia — CrossFire Stars 2024](https://liquipedia.net/crossfire/CrossFire_Stars/2024)

### Men’s Dota 2
Page: https://goat.biblioverse.org/en/#m/dota-2-masculino
- GOAT: Johan “N0tail” Sundstein (DK)
- Legends: Topias “Topson” Taavitsainen (FI), Clement “Puppey” Ivanov (EE), Illya “Yatoro” Mulyarchuk (UA), Magomed “Collapse” Khalilov (RU)
- Stars: Kuro “KuroKy” Takhasomi (DE), Anathan “ana” Pham (AU), Sébastien “Ceb” Debs (FR), Jesse “JerAx” Vainikka (FI), Myroslav “Mira” Kolpakov (UA), Yaroslav “Miposhka” Naidenov (UA), Neta “33” Shapira (IL), Danil “Dendi” Ishutin (UA), Oleksandr “XBOCT” Dashkevych (UA)
- Other greats: Michał “Nisha” Jankowski (PL), Zhang “y`” Yiping (CN), Martin “Saksa” Sazdov (SE), Amer “Miracle-” Al-Barkawi (JO), Xu “fy” Linsen (CN), Ludwig “zai” Wåhlberg (SE), Wang “Ame” Chunyu (CN), Leon “Nine” Kirilin (RU), Artour “Arteezy” Babaev (CA), Gustav “s4” Magnusson (SE)
- Fact-check: high

Johan “N0tail” Sundstein captained OG, which made history by winning two straight editions of The International (2018 and 2019), with unique leadership, versatility and longevity. In 2026, however, Yatoro and Collapse became the first three-time TI champions, with Team Spirit (2021, 2023 and 2026) — and are already contending for the title of greatest of all.

### Dragon Ball FighterZ

- GOAT: Goichi “GO1” Kishida (JP)
- Legends: Dominique “SonicFox” McLean (US)
- Stars: Kazunoko (JP), Fenritti (JP)
- Fact-check: low

GO1 is the most successful Dragon Ball FighterZ player: champion of EVO 2019, beating SonicFox in the final, and of the 2020 World Tour Finals. SonicFox won the game’s first EVO, in 2018, and is an eight-time EVO champion across different titles. In recent years, Hikari won the World Tour Finals in 2024 and 2025.

### GeoGuessr

- GOAT: no consensus yet
- Fact-check: medium

No consensus: in four editions, the GeoGuessr world championship has had four different champions. Blinky is the most consistent name — champion in 2024 and runner-up in 2023 and 2026, with a record three finals. Consus won the first World Cup (2023), Radu C was champion in 2025, and Debre, runner-up in 2025, took the title in 2026.

### Honor of Kings

- GOAT: Peng “Fly” Yunfei (CN)
- Legends: Xu “YiNuo” Bicheng (CN)
- Fact-check: medium

Honor of Kings is China’s most popular mobile game. Fly holds the record of six professional finals MVP awards (Guinness), with titles in the KPL and the World Champion Cup. YiNuo is the game’s all-time top earner and won the 2025 World Cup and two KPL finals, taking two finals MVPs.

### Men’s League of Legends
Page: https://goat.biblioverse.org/en/#m/league-of-legends-masculino
- GOAT: Lee “Faker” Sang-hyeok (KR)
- Legends: Jian “Uzi” Zihao (CN), Rasmus “Caps” Winther (DK), Bae “Bengi” Seong-woong (KR), Cho “Mata” Se-hyeong (KR)
- Stars: Kang “TheShy” Seung-lok (KR), Park “Ruler” Jae-hyuk (KR), Ryu “Keria” Min-seok (KR), Lee “Gumayusi” Min-hyeong (KR), Moon “Oner” Hyeon-jun (KR), Choi “Zeus” Woo-je (KR), Kim “Canyon” Geon-bu (KR)
- Other greats: Luka “Perkz” Perković (HR), Carl Martin Erik “Rekkles” Larsson (SE), Kim “Doinb” Tae-sang (KR), Song “Rookie” Eui-jin (KR), Jo “CoreJJ” Yong-in (KR), Heo “ShowMaker” Su (KR), Kim “Deft” Hyuk-kyu (KR), Kang “Ambition” Chan-yong (KR)
- Fact-check: high

Lee “Faker” Sang-hyeok is widely considered the greatest player in League of Legends history: he holds the record of six world titles (2013, 2015, 2016, 2023, 2024 and 2025) — the first to win three in a row — plus ten LCK titles, two MSIs, two Worlds Finals MVPs and Asian Games gold in 2022 and 2026, always with T1, who are defending a four-peat at the 2026 World Championship in the US. He was the first name in Riot’s Hall of Legends (2024), followed by Uzi (2025), China’s most celebrated marksman, and by Caps, the greatest Western player. Bengi has three world titles alongside Faker, and Mata, 2014 champion and MVP, is called the greatest support ever. From T1’s three-peat, Keria, Gumayusi (2025 Finals MVP) and Oner also have three world titles.

Sources:
- [GosuGamers](https://www.gosugamers.net/lol/news/77576-t1-claim-sixth-title-with-third-consecutive-victory-as-the-worlds-2025-champions)

### Rainbow Six Siege
Page: https://goat.biblioverse.org/en/#m/rainbow-six-siege
- GOAT: Niclas “Pengu” Mouritzen (DK)
- Legends: Luccas “Paluh” Molina (BR), Stéphane “Shaiiko” Lebleu (FR), Lucas “soulz1” Schinke (BR)
- Stars: Nathanial “Rampy” Duvall (US), Jason “Beaulo” Doty (US), Loïc “BriD” Chongthep (FR), Ben “CTZN” McMillan (GB), Gustavo “HerdsZ” Herdina (BR), Diego “Kheyze” Zanello (BR), João “Jv92” Vitor (BR), Handyy (BR)
- Other greats: Karl “Alem4o” Zarth (BR), Paul “Hyper” Kontopanagiotis (US), Gustavo “Psycho” Rigal (BR), Matthew “Achieved” Solomon (US), Benjamin “Benjamaster” Dereli (DK), Felipe “nade” Ferreira (BR), Juhani “Kantoraketti” Toivonen (FI)
- Fact-check: high

Niclas “Pengu” Mouritzen is the most decorated player in Rainbow Six history: he won back-to-back Six Invitationals (2018 and 2019), the Paris Major and four Pro League seasons before retiring in 2021. In 2025 and 2026, FaZe Clan became the first back-to-back Invitational champion.

### Rocket League
Page: https://goat.biblioverse.org/en/#m/rocket-league
- GOAT: Alexandre “Kaydop” Courant (FR), Pierre “Turbopolsa” Silfver (SE)
- Stars: Jos “ViolentPanda” van Meurs (NL), Evan “M0nkey M00n” Rogez (FR), Amine “zen” Benayachi (FR)
- Other greats: Saleh “Rw9” Bakhashwin (SA), Samy “dralii” Hajji (MA)
- Prospects: Kiileerrz (SA)
- Fact-check: medium

Pierre “Turbopolsa” Silfver is the most successful RLCS champion, with four world titles (seasons 3, 4, 5 and 8) with three different teams — about half of all world championships at the time. Alexandre “Kaydop” Courant has three, two of them alongside Turbopolsa. In the recent era, M0nkey M00n won two world titles with BDS (2022 and 2024), zen was champion and MVP with Vitality in 2023, NRG won in 2025 and, in 2026, the Falcons of Rw9 (finals MVP) and Kiileerrz (tournament MVP) gave the Middle East its first world title, with dralii reaching his second.

Sources:
- [Rocket League — Becoming a Legend: Turbopolsa](https://www.rocketleague.com/news/becoming-a-legend-turbopolsa)
- [Wikipédia (EN): Rocket League Championship Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_League_Championship_Series)
- [Esports Insider — NRG campeã mundial de 2025](https://esportsinsider.com/2025/09/nrg-rlcs-world-championship-2025-win)
- [Sheep Esports — Falcons campeã mundial de 2026](https://www.sheepesports.com/en/articles/team-falcons-dismantle-spacestation-gaming-to-win-the-rlcs-2026-world-championship/en)
- [esports.gg — resultados do mundial de 2026](https://esports.gg/news/rocket-league/rlcs-2026-world-championship-finals-overview-results/)

### Sim Racing
Page: https://goat.biblioverse.org/en/#m/automobilismo-virtual-sim-racing
- GOAT: Jarno Opmeer (NL)
- Legends: Brendon Leigh (GB)
- Stars: Frederik Rasmussen (DK), Igor Fraga (BR)
- Fact-check: low

Jarno Opmeer holds the record of three F1 Sim Racing World Championship titles, the main virtual motorsport championship. Brendon Leigh won two (2017 and 2018), and Brazil’s Igor Fraga, a Gran Turismo world champion, took his virtual success to real racetracks.

Sources:
- [Fanatec — tricampeonato de Opmeer](https://www.fanatec.com/us/en/explorer/games/gaming-tips/opmeer-f1-sim-racing-world-championship/)
- [Wikipédia (EN): F1 Sim Racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F1_Sim_Racing)

### StarCraft
Page: https://goat.biblioverse.org/en/#m/starcraft
- GOAT: Lee “Flash” Young-ho (KR)
- Legends: Joona “Serral” Sotala (FI), Lee “Jaedong” Jae-dong (KR)
- Stars: Lim “BoxeR” Yo-hwan (KR), Cho “Maru” Seong-ju (KR), Lee “Rogue” Byung-ryul (KR)
- Other greats: Song “Bisu” Byung-goo (KR)
- Fact-check: medium

Flash, the “God” of StarCraft: Brood War, had a 70% win rate in every matchup and the longest reign as No. 1. Serral is the biggest name in StarCraft II and remains dominant: in 2026 he won Maestros of the Game 2, HomeStory Cup XXIX and RSL Revival.

Sources:
- [Liquipedia](https://www.liquipedia.net/starcraft/Flash)

### Street Fighter
Page: https://goat.biblioverse.org/en/#m/street-fighter
- GOAT: Daigo Umehara (JP)
- Legends: Justin Wong (US), Hajime “Tokido” Taniguchi (JP)
- Stars: Saul “MenaRD” Segundo (DO), Shinya “Nuki” Onuki (JP), Victor “Punk” Woodley (US)
- Fact-check: medium

Daigo Umehara, author of the legendary “Evo Moment 37” (2004), is the biggest name in Street Fighter history: he has six EVO titles and the Guinness record for the most successful player in the series’ major tournaments. Justin Wong, his opponent in that match, has eight EVO titles across several games. In the Street Fighter 6 era, the Dominican MenaRD is the great champion.

Sources:
- [Wikipédia (EN): Daigo Umehara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daigo_Umehara)
- [Wikipédia (EN): Evo Moment 37](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evo_Moment_37)
- [Wikipédia (EN): Justin Wong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Wong)
- [Wikipédia (EN): campeões do EVO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Evolution_Championship_Series_champions)

- GOAT: Joseph “Mang0” Marquez (US), Leonardo “MkLeo” López (MX)
- Legends: Adam “Armada” Lindgren (SE), Juan “Hungrybox” Debiedma (US)
- Stars: Jason “Mew2King” Zimmerman (US), Kevin “PPMD” Nanney (US), Gonzalo “ZeRo” Barrios (CL)
- Other greats: Zain Naghmi (US)
- Fact-check: medium

Mang0 has more than 30 major titles in Melee and leads the debate with Armada. MkLeo is considered the greatest Smash Ultimate player.

### Tekken
Page: https://goat.biblioverse.org/en/#m/tekken
- GOAT: Arslan Ash (PK)
- Legends: Jae-min “Knee” Bae (KR)
- Stars: Rangchu (KR)
- Fact-check: medium

Pakistan’s Arslan Ash is named the greatest Tekken player: he won Tekken 8 at EVO 2026, against South Korea’s Rangchu, reaching eight EVO titles, and is the only Tekken 7 triple-crown champion (EVO, EVO Japan and the Tekken World Tour Finals). Knee, the South Korean legend, won his fourth EVO title in 2025 at age 39, a longevity record.

Sources:
- [Liquipedia — Arslan Ash](https://liquipedia.net/fighters/Arslan_Ash)

### Valorant (Inclusive)
Page: https://goat.biblioverse.org/en/#m/valorant-feminino-inclusivo-game-changers
- GOAT: Ava “florescent” Eugene (US)
- Legends: Michaela “mimi” Lintrup (DK), Alexis “alexis” Guarrasi (US), Paula “bstrdd” Naguil (CL), Natália “daiki” Vilela (BR)
- Stars: Maryam “Mary” Maher (BH), Constanza “conir” Reyes (CL), Melanie “meL” Capone (US)
- Other greats: Petra “Petra” Stoker (NL), Anastasiya “Glance” Anisimova (RU), Lorrian “Lorri” Elad (PH)
- Fact-check: high

Ava “florescent” Eugene is considered the player with the best aim in the competitive Game Changers scene. She is known for exceptional skill and an aggressive playstyle, standing out at major events as a duelist with agents like Jett. In 2023 she led Shopify Rebellion to the Game Changers Championship, the world title of the inclusive Valorant scene.

### Valorant (Mixed)
Page: https://goat.biblioverse.org/en/#m/valorant
- GOAT: Erick “aspas” Santos (BR)
- Legends: Zheng “ZmjjKK” Yongkang (CN), Max “Demon1” Mazanov (US), Tyson “TenZ” Ngo (CA), Timofey “Chronicle” Khromov (RU)
- Stars: Nikita “Derke” Sirmitev (FI), Jaccob “yay” Whiteaker (US), Roberto “erde” Lobos (CL), Brock “brawk” Somerhalder (US), Jason “f0rsakeN” Susanto (ID), Ethan “Ethan” Arnold (US)
- Other greats: Aleksander “zeek” Zygmunt (PL), N4RRATE (US), sScary (FR), Asuna (US), Gustavo “Sacy” Rossi (BR), Kim “Meteor” Tae-oh (KR), Dambi (KR), Matías “Saadhak” Delipetro (AR)
- Prospects: Lucca “Luk xo” Travaioli (BR)
- Fact-check: high

Erick “aspas” Santos is considered by many the best player in Valorant history: a sharp-aiming duelist, he won the world title with LOUD at Champions 2022 and became a symbol of the Brazilian scene. Ethan Arnold was the first player to win two Champions titles, with Evil Geniuses (2023) and, by then as in-game leader, with NRG (2025). Timofey “Chronicle” Khromov holds the VCT record for international titles, with three: Masters Berlin 2021 with Gambit, and LOCK//IN 2023 and Masters Tokyo 2023 with Fnatic, where he was named MVP. Matías “Saadhak” Delipetro was the in-game leader of LOUD’s 2022 world-champion team. In recent years international titles have spread out: NRG at Champions 2025 (MVP brawk), LOUD at Champions 2026 — the first organization to win two world titles, with erde as MVP and 19-year-old Lucca “Luk xo” Travaioli as a standout, after he became the first player to get five quadra kills in a single series on the circuit —, T1 and Paper Rex at the 2025 Masters, and Nongshim RedForce and LEVIATÁN at the 2026 Masters.
